newsitem.title: USA: ATHLETICS-JOHNSON READY FOR FAST RUN AT WORLD CHAMPIONSHIPS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-JOHNSON READY FOR FAST RUN AT WORLD CHAMPIONSHIPS.

text.p: Double Olympic champion Michael Johnson has sent a warning to those with visions of claiming his world 400 metres title in Athens next month.
Now that he has a special "wild card" invitation to next month's world championships, the Athens 400 metres final will be no ordinary race, Johnson said on Monday.
"It would not do me any good to just try to get back to running 43.9 or 44 flat," Johnson, world and Olympic 200 and 400 metres gold medallist, said.
Loftier goals are on his mind, goals like the 43.29 world record for the 400 metres set by fellow American Butch Reynolds in 1988.

Johnson strained his left quadriceps in a 150 metres race against Olympic champion Donovan Bailey in Toronto on June 1 and finished a demoralising fifth in a 400 metres event in Paris on June 25. He plans to make the world championships his first race back.
"Prior to the injury I felt I was on target to run a very low 43, if not 42, and that's the kind of shape I'm trying to get into now," Johnson said.
"I would not be going (to the world championships) unless I was 100 percent healthy.
"If I go out and run my kind of race, a smart race, I cannot be beat."

Conceding that he was probably the moving force behind the decision of the International Amateur Athletic Federation (IAAF) to grant wild cards to all defending world champions, Johnson said: "It's an honour to be treated that way.

"I feel they (the wild cards) probably came about because of what happened in Toronto," he said of the injury which forced him to miss the U.S. championships, selection meeting for world championships.
"They (IAAF leaders) felt they needed me there and I felt like I should be there."
Although some, including IAAF vice-president Arne Ljungqvist of Sweden, are opposed to the way the wild-card entries were approved, Johnson said he believed they would prove invaluable.
"It ensures that we have great match-ups, it ensures that we have marquee names," he said.
But it remained unclear whether all American world champions who received wild cards would compete in their events.

Brad Hunt, Johnson's agent who also represents world champions Dan O'Brien and Gwen Torrence, said decathlon world record-holder O'Brien would undergo a bone scan for a possible stress fracture on Tuesday before deciding whether to compete.
Bob Kersee, coach of women's world 100 metres hurdles champion Gail Devers, told reporters: "If she (Devers) gets on the (4x100 metres relay) I won't have her run the hurdles."
U.S. women's team coach Gary Winckler said Devers, who pulled out of the U.S. 100 metres final citing injury, would be a member of the U.S. relay pool.
However, he declined to offer a relay spot to Torrence, the defending women's world 100 metres champion, because she did not attend the U.S. championships.
"But my decision could easily be overriden by others," Winckler added.
U.S. men's team coach Dean Hayes said he would probably add Johnson to the American 4x400 metres relay pool but wanted clarification from IAAF officials on Johnson's relay status before doing so.
Johnson said he would enjoy being a part of the relay.
But the speedy Texan said he also had another assignment for Athens. Following his projected 400 metres final, he is to join the NBC television crew for its coverage of the world championships.
